module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 101

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Definitions

The **$\alpha$-core** of a graph $G$, written `alphaCore G`, is the set of vertices
$v$ such that removing $v$ strictly decreases the independence number:
$$\mathrm{alphaCore}(G) = \{v \mid \alpha(G - v) < \alpha(G)\}$$
where $G - v$ is the subgraph of $G$ induced on $V(G) \setminus \{v\}$.

These vertices are also called "critical vertices for independence."
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture101

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/-- The independence number of the subgraph induced on $V \setminus \{v\}$
(i.e., the graph $G - v$). -/
noncomputable def indepNumDeleteVertex (G : SimpleGraph α) (v : α) : ℕ :=
  (G.induce (Set.univ \ {v})).indepNum

/-- The $\alpha$-core of $G$: the set of vertices whose removal strictly decreases the
independence number. A vertex $v$ is in the $\alpha$-core if $\alpha(G - v) < \alpha(G)$. -/
noncomputable def alphaCore (G : SimpleGraph α) : Finset α :=
  Finset.univ.filter (fun v => indepNumDeleteVertex G v < G.indepNum)

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 101](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$,
$\alpha(G) \le \lfloor (n + |\mathrm{alphaCore}(G)|) / 2 \rfloor$
where $\alpha(G) = G.\mathrm{indepNum}$ is the independence number, $n$ is the
number of vertices, and $\mathrm{alphaCore}(G)$ is the set of vertices whose
removal decreases the independence number.

This is a theorem known to follow from inclusion-exclusion principles.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture101 (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected) :
    G.indepNum ≤ (Fintype.card α + (alphaCore G).card) / 2 := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The $\alpha$-core has cardinality at most $n$ (the number of vertices). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : (alphaCore G).card ≤ 3 := by
  apply Finset.card_le_univ

/-- The $\alpha$-core is always a subset of all vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)) : alphaCore G ⊆ Finset.univ :=
  Finset.filter_subset _ _

/-- If a vertex $v$ is NOT in the $\alpha$-core, then removing $v$ does not decrease $\alpha$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (v : Fin 3)
    (hv : v ∉ alphaCore G) :
    G.indepNum ≤ indepNumDeleteVertex G v := by
  unfold alphaCore at hv
  simp [Finset.mem_filter] at hv
  exact hv

/-- If a vertex $v$ IS in the $\alpha$-core, then removing $v$ strictly decreases $\alpha$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (v : Fin 3)
    (hv : v ∈ alphaCore G) :
    indepNumDeleteVertex G v < G.indepNum := by
  unfold alphaCore at hv
  exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hv).2

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture101

reformulations.difference: The source defines alphacore(G) as the cardinality of the intersection of all maximum independent sets. Lean defines a Finset of vertices whose deletion strictly decreases the independence number, and uses its cardinality in conjecture101.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite graph, deleting v cannot increase the independence number. It preserves that number exactly when some maximum independent set avoids v. Thus deletion strictly decreases it exactly when v belongs to every maximum independent set. Proved the membership biconditional in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, including its formulation with G.IsMaximumIndepSet.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires [Nontrivial α], whereas the source says simply that G is a simple connected graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only omitted connected case is the one-vertex graph. Its independence number and core cardinality are both 1, so the claimed inequality is 1 ≤ (1 + 1) / 2. Proved this case for arbitrary singleton vertex types and proved the equivalence between the unrestricted connected-graph statement and the Lean restrictions in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. The decidability instances impose no classical mathematical restriction.

review.notes: Checked both definitions, the main theorem, and all four sanity checks. The source states the same bound, marks Conjecture 101 'T' (true), and gives the inclusion–exclusion remark, agreeing with the file's solved status. Natural-number division by 2 correctly implements the source's floor. Both scratch files compile successfully; boundary computations covered the empty graph, singleton, complete graphs, an edgeless three-vertex graph, P3, and C5. The equivalence proofs do not depend on sorry. The live source timed out, so archived primary-source pages were used.
